🏛️ The results are in. So what happens next in your council?

1️⃣ Coalition talks: 137 of 213 councils are hung, including seven of the eight metros. Parties now negotiate who works with whom.
2️⃣ First meeting: each new council must meet within 14 days of the results being declared. The municipal manager calls the meeting.
3️⃣ The vote: at that first sitting, councillors elect a speaker and a mayor. In a hung council, the mayor needs the votes of more than half the councillors, so the coalition deal decides who wins.
4️⃣ The budget: the mayor tables a draft budget around March, residents can comment, and council must approve it before 1 July.
5️⃣ Your bill: the new rates, water, refuse and electricity tariffs start on 1 July 2027.

Why it matters: a stable coalition passes budgets on time. A shaky one can delay repairs and services.

Who would you trust to run your city's budget? 👇

text:
🏛️ Hung councils are back. So what happens if a council can't agree on a budget?

1️⃣ The deadline: every municipality must approve its budget, with its new rates and tariffs, before the financial year starts on 1 July (Municipal Finance Management Act).
2️⃣ If council fails, the mayor must call it back to try again.
3️⃣ If it still fails, the province must intervene (Constitution, section 139(4)). That can include dissolving the council and approving a temporary budget until a new council is elected.
4️⃣ Until a budget is in place, the municipality can only spend money with the provincial finance MEC's approval, within strict limits.

What it means for you: a deadlock rarely changes your rates overnight, but it can delay repairs, new projects and supplier payments, and that shows up in your water, roads and lights first.

🇺🇸 The US says South Africa will lose its AGOA trade benefits from 1 January 2027.

What is AGOA? The African Growth and Opportunity Act lets eligible African countries sell many goods to the US without import duties. South Africa uses it for cars, fruit, wine and other products.

What happened: on 2 November, the US Trade Representative said President Trump had told Congress he intends to end South Africa's (and Rwanda's) eligibility. The US cited trade barriers, corruption and its own security and foreign-policy interests, and said eligibility could be restored if those concerns are addressed.

What it means at home: exporters face the normal US duties on top of existing tariffs, which puts pressure on jobs in farming and manufacturing, especially in the Eastern Cape and Western Cape. Government says it is still talking to Washington.

👷 Stats SA publishes the next unemployment figures this month. Here's where we stand going in.

In the second quarter of 2026 (April to June):
📈 The official unemployment rate rose to 33.6%, up from 32.7%.
👥 8.5 million people were unemployed, 345,000 more than in the first quarter.
🧑 Youth (15 to 34) unemployment was 47.4%.
🗺️ The Eastern Cape had the highest rate at 47.5%.

What it means for households: fewer jobs means fewer earners per home, more pressure on grants, and less spending at local businesses. It also matters to the Reserve Bank, which weighs a weak economy against inflation when it sets rates on 19 November.

🛍️ Black Friday is on 27 November. Five checks before you swipe:

1️⃣ Make your list now, before the adverts start. Buy what you planned, not what's flashing.
2️⃣ Note today's price of what you want. Some "specials" were cheaper two weeks earlier.
3️⃣ On credit, look at the total cost: the instalment times the months, plus fees and interest. A low monthly figure can hide a high price.
4️⃣ Think twice before opening a new store card for a once-off discount. It's new debt, and it shows on your credit record.
5️⃣ Remember January: school fees, uniforms and the long wait to payday after December.

General information, not financial advice.

⛽ Early signs for December: petrol could get cheaper, diesel may not.

Central Energy Fund data for the first week of November shows petrol over-recovering by about R2 a litre. That means, if it holds, a cut is likely on the first Wednesday of December. Oil prices have fallen and the rand has firmed to around R16.50 to the dollar.

Two things can shrink the cut:
➖ The temporary fuel levy relief gets smaller in December, so part of the saving goes back to the levy.
➖ Diesel is tracking higher in some early estimates.

This is a forecast, not an official price. The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources announces the real numbers at the end of the month.

text:
🏠 How is your property rates bill worked out? It's one simple sum:

(Your property's municipal value − R15,000) × the council's rate in the rand = your rates for the year

🔹 Municipal value: what the city's valuation roll says your home is worth. You can object when a new roll comes out.
🔹 The first R15,000 of a home's value can't be rated, by law. Many metros exclude more than that, and offer pensioner and indigent rebates.
🔹 Rate in the rand: set by your council in its budget every year.

Example (illustrative rate): a R1 million home at 0.01 in the rand → (R1,000,000 − R15,000) × 0.01 = R9,850 a year, about R821 a month.

That's why the councils elected this month matter: they set that rate from July 2027.

Do you know your home's municipal value? 👇

#MzansiMoneyMatters #PropertyRates #LGE2026
